transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time. I guess what brings me in is just that my sleep has gotten a little... messed up lately. It's probably nothing too serious, but I'll either stay up half the night with my mind just kind of running, or I'll wake up way too early feeling like I never really rested. 

I'm sure a lot of people deal with that, right? I just wanted to see if maybe I could get some advice on it, if that's okay?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, especially around the time you’re trying to sleep?

Um, no, I don't think so? I hope I'm answering that right. It's not really... worry, I guess. Like, I'm not lying there stressing about work—I do bookkeeping, so there's always numbers to think about, but I'm not anxious about them or anything. 

It's more just that my brain is, you know, just kind of going. But I'm not having panic attacks or feeling super stressed out. I try really hard not to be a worrier, actually. I hope that's okay? I just don't want to make it sound like I'm complaining about being anxious when I'm really not. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself feeling tired or sleepy during the day, even after you’ve had some sleep?

Um, a little bit, maybe? I really don't want to sound lazy or anything, because I know everyone works hard, but... yeah, I guess I do get pretty tired. Even after I've been in bed for a full night, just walking from the parking lot into the office... it almost feels like I'm dragging sandbags? And then by lunchtime, my brain just feels completely worn out. 

I mean, I'm sure everyone gets that afternoon slump, right? I try really hard to just push through it, so it's not like I'm falling asleep at my desk or doing a bad job at work. I hope it's okay to admit that I get that tired? I just really don't want you to think I'm slacking off.
How often do these difficulties with falling asleep or waking up too early happen? Do they happen most nights, or only occasionally?

Um, I guess it's... maybe a few times a week? I really haven't kept a strict log or anything, so I hope I'm not giving you bad information. It's definitely not every single night. 

Sometimes I'll have a couple of nights in a row where I just can't seem to settle down, or I wake up at three in the morning and that's it. But then I'll have a night where I sleep okay, I think. I mean, it's enough to bother me, obviously, since I'm here, but I don't want to make it sound like I never sleep at all. That would be exaggerating, and I definitely don't want to do that. Is a few times a week normal for someone coming in to see you?
Do you usually feel refreshed when you wake up, or does it feel like you haven’t really rested even after sleeping?

Um, no, not really refreshed. I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just complaining about being tired all the time, but... yeah, that's actually kind of the main reason I came in. My sleep has just gotten so messed up lately. 

Like I was saying, I'll either be up half the night with my mind just kind of running, or I'll wake up way too early. And when I do wake up, even if I got a few hours, it just feels like I haven't really rested at all. It's like my brain didn't actually turn off? I really try to just drink some coffee and put a smile on at work, but it's getting kind of hard. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up as such a big issue? I just really want to figure out how to get back to sleeping normally so I can do a good job during the day.
Even when you do sleep for a few hours, does it still feel like you haven’t truly rested at all?

Um, well, it's actually kind of the opposite sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound inconsistent, since I was just saying how tired I am during the day. But... yeah, there have been several nights recently where I only slept, like, three or four hours total. 

And the weird thing is, when I woke up, I didn't feel tired at all. I actually felt really charged up? Like, I didn't even need my morning coffee, which is super unusual for me. I felt like I could just jump right into my day and get a ton of bookkeeping done. Is that... is that a bad thing to admit? I mean, I know you're supposed to get eight hours, so I don't want you to think I'm purposely staying up or neglecting my health. It's just that my body seemed totally fine with it on those days. Does that make sense?

On the days when you only slept three or four hours but felt really energized and ready to go, did you also find yourself needing less sleep than usual, like your body just didn’t seem to require as much rest?

Um, yeah, I guess that's exactly it. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm trying to be difficult by saying I'm exhausted but then also saying I don't need sleep. I know it's confusing. But, um, yeah, there were definitely several nights where I only got those three or four hours, and I just... I didn't feel like I needed more? 

It wasn't like I was forcing myself out of bed. I just woke up and felt completely charged, like I was ready to tackle everything. I didn't even need my coffee, which, like I said, is just so not me. It really felt like my body just decided it had enough rest and didn't require any more. I hope you don't think I'm making this up or being dramatic? It's just so weird to feel so energized on so little sleep, but that's really how it happened. Is it okay that I'm explaining it this way?

During those days when you felt really energized and didn’t need much sleep, did you also notice your mood being unusually high, irritable, or elevated—like feeling overly confident, restless, or more easily annoyed than usual?

Um, well... I guess maybe my mood was a little different? I really hope I don't sound like a terrible person for saying this, but... yeah, earlier in the month, I did feel kind of, I don't know, almost lit up? Like I was just completely unstoppable and doing such a great job at work. 

But then... I don't want you to think I'm normally like this, because I really try to be nice to everyone, but I did find myself getting a little snappy. Like, my mom or my supervisor would ask me these tiny little questions that usually wouldn't bother me at all, and I just... I'd snap at them. I felt so bad about it afterward. I just felt kind of restless and on edge, I guess? I hope you don't think I'm just a difficult employee or a bad daughter. It just felt like I had all this energy and nowhere to put it, so I got annoyed faster than I should have. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes?
Did you have a period lasting several days where your mood was consistently elevated, irritable, or you felt unusually energetic, even beyond just feeling good about your work performance?

Um, well... I guess I did have a few days like that, yeah. I hope it doesn't sound like I was just being manic or something crazy, because I was actually being really productive! But... um, yeah, for a while there I just had this huge burst of energy. 

Like, I'd get home from work—and usually I'm so tired after staring at spreadsheets all day—but I'd just start cleaning everything. And then I started making all these lists for home renovations, and I was looking up interest rates, and even trying to set up ideas for a side job? All in the same evening. It was like I just couldn't shut my brain off. I was getting so much done, which is a good thing, right? I just... I hope you don't think I was acting completely out of control. I was just really motivated for a few days. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Was there a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable for at least four days in a row, not just momentary spikes but a consistent mood change?

Um, yeah... I guess it was definitely for at least four days in a row. I hope I'm explaining this right, but... yeah, it wasn't just a quick thing. 

The really obvious back-and-forth—like, cycling between that super charged-up stretch where I was doing all the renovations and lists, and then this awful crash where I just feel so low... it's been going on for about a month now? I think it really started when getting a mortgage became a real thing we were doing. I know buying a house is stressful for everyone, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just overreacting to normal life stuff. But yeah, that consistent change... it lasted for several days at a time before I crashed. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable for at least a full week—not just a few days—where it was clearly different from how you normally feel?

Um, no, I don't think it ever lasted a full week. I hope that's okay to say? Like, I definitely had those few days where I was super productive and maybe a little on edge, but it was never, like, seven whole days in a row. Usually by day four or five, I would just kind of... run out of steam, I guess? And then I'd be back to feeling really down and tired. 

I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, and I don't think I've ever been stuck like that for a whole week. Is it better that it only lasted a few days? I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right picture.

Have there been times when you felt down or really low most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had other symptoms like changes in your appetite, trouble concentrating, or feeling hopeless?

Um, well... yes. I hope it's okay to admit that, but yeah, I've definitely been having those low times too. I don't want you to think I'm just complaining or ungrateful, because I know I have a lot going for me, but... lately, I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling. 

It's hard to explain without sounding silly, but... even when I'm just sitting in my own condo, the one I worked so hard to get, it just makes me want to cry. I don't know why I get like that. I should be happy, right? But I just feel so down most of the day, and it's hard to focus on my bookkeeping work when I feel that way. I'm really trying my best to push through it, though. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you had a period of time lasting two weeks or more where you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, even when there was no clear reason for it?

Um, yeah, I guess it's been going on for a while. I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it, but... well, that heavy, kind of guilty fog? It's been hanging around for, um, about five months now. 

I know I mentioned it got a lot worse after I actually bought the condo, and I know that's supposed to be a happy thing, so I feel terrible even saying this. But honestly, it's been there most days for those five months. Even when I try really hard to shake it off, it just... stays. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this? I don't want to sound like a whiner, I just want to make sure you have all the facts.

During that time when you felt unusually energetic and needed less sleep, did you have a period lasting at least four days where you felt abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood along with increased goal-directed activity like doing multiple projects at once or taking on too many tasks?

Um, yeah... I think so? I mean, earlier in the month, for maybe four or five days, I just felt... I don't know, almost lit up? Like I was totally unstoppable and could get a million things done at work and at home. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging, because I really liked feeling that way, it felt good to be so productive. 

But... well, I also felt kind of, um, on edge? I feel really bad admitting this, but I actually snapped at my mom a few times. And even my supervisor at work. They would just ask me little questions that normally wouldn't bother me at all, and I just got so irritated so fast. I'm usually really polite, I promise! I just... I couldn't help it during those few days. I hope you don't think I'm a mean person for that. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Did you have a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable for at least four days in a row, along with doing more activities than usual or taking on too many tasks at once?

Um, well, yes... I think so. I really hope I'm answering this right, but... yeah, during those few days, I just had this huge burst of energy. I don't want it to sound like I was being manic or anything crazy, I just... I was getting so much done. 

Like, after I'd finish my bookkeeping work for the day, I couldn't just relax. I'd start deep cleaning my condo, and then I was making all these big lists for renovations I want to do, and checking out interest rates online... I even started setting up ideas for a side job. It was like I just couldn't shut my brain off, but in a good way? I mean, I was just trying to be productive and make the most of my time. I hope that's a normal thing to do? I just didn't want to waste all that energy, you know?

Can you confirm if there was a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable for at least four full days in a row, where your mood was clearly different from how you usually feel when you're not depressed?

Um, yes, I think that's exactly what I meant. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... yeah, it was definitely for at least four days straight earlier this month. 

It was just like I said, I felt... I don't know, almost lit up? Like I was just totally unstoppable and feeling really, really good. Which I guess is a nice thing, right? I just felt so capable. But then... well, it was different from my normal self because of the irritable part. Like I mentioned, I ended up snapping at my mom, and even my supervisor, just over these really tiny questions. I'm usually so careful not to be rude to people, so it was definitely out of character for me. I just... I felt so on edge during that time, even though I also felt great. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
